messages:
jen: Seeing a sudden p95 jump in hosted-eu around 16:03 UTC. p95 210ms -> ~1.9s, p99 ~4.6s. Anyone on this?

infra-bot: alert: hosted-eu p95 breach detected (5m). Grafana: https://grafana.company/reports/hosted-eu-p95

sam: I'm on it. Traces show queue depth rising on model-pool-3, backlog ~200 reqs. ratecap didn't change. Might be batching heuristic oscillation.

ravi: looking at kselector logs — rapid kernel flips started at spike start, fp16 -> aux -> fp16 within seconds. suspicious for short-seq mispredict.

lisa: KV cache hit-rate dropped 92% -> 65% at 16:01, prefetch churn spiked. Missing prefix priming.

sam: profiler snippet (tail):
```
16:01:02 runtime/queue.go: enqueue depth=198
16:01:03 runtime/kselector.go: choose_kernel: seq_len=8 -> selected=aux (latency_penalty=1.8)
16:01:03 runtime/batcher.go: coalesce windows increased from 20ms -> 110ms
16:01:04 runtime/kvcache.go: miss_rate=0.35
```

mauro: tenant "client-42" had a burst ~1.3k rps starting 16:00. Their traffic is very short-seq heavy. Could be noisy neighbor causing priming churn. @ops can you confirm?

ops: confirmed. client-42 kicked off a ramping job, sustained burst for ~3 mins. We applied soft throttle at 16:05 and isolated to a dedicated pool.

jen: mitigation: throttled tenant, rolled back yesterday's kselector tweak on hosted-eu. seeing p95 drop to ~250ms within 90s.

sam: proposed follow-ups: add guard to avoid kernel flip when queue_depth > 50 && shortseq_fraction > 30%. Also add KV-prefetch backoff when cache_miss_rate > 20% to prevent churn amplifying latency.

ravi: will open a small PR for kselector: record flip_reason and timestamp, expose metric `kselector.flip_reasons` for alerting.

lisa: I'll add a short regression eval simulating noisy-tenant short-seq bursts and validate autoscale + batch smoothing behavior.

deploy-bot: rolled back kselector v1.12 -> v1.11 on hosted-eu at 16:07 by @jen.

jen: monitoring. If p99 stays < 2s after 10m we'll close the thread. Thanks everyone :heart:
